clinician.final_diagnosis: the inflammatory nature of the axillary lymphadenopathies was confirmed
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old female presented for annual mammographic screening, which revealed many enlarged bilateral axillary lymph nodes without suspicious breast findings. She reported no breast/axillary symptoms or recent vaccinations, and had no prior axillary adenopathy in 2017. Subsequent ultrasound confirmed numerous enlarged lymph nodes with Doppler signal showing intra- and extranodal vascularization, favoring an active inflammatory process. The patient's medical history included mixed connective tissue disease and psoriatic arthropathy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Mammography demonstrated many enlarged axillary lymph nodes bilaterally, with no suspicious breast findings.
Ultrasound confirmed numerous enlarged lymph nodes with Doppler signal showing intra- and extranodal vascularization, playing in favour of an active inflammatory process.
Patient has a history of mixed connective tissue disease and psoriatic arthropathy.
